public_rationale: SiliconData's August 27, 2026 methodology describes adjustments for on-demand, reserved and interruptible rentals, followed by aggregation and weighting across providers [e1]. Its March 12 explanation also describes normalizing different rental structures, including multi-year reserved contracts [e2]. These disclosures do not provide the effective rental-term weights or adjustment coefficients needed to determine whether immediate rental prices overwhelmingly influenced the index on October 13, 2026 [e1, e2]. Including reserved contracts alone does not settle their influence [e1, e2].
limitations: The disclosures do not provide a dated audit of input composition and effective influence for October 13, 2026 [e1, e2].
Provider aggregation and rental-type coverage do not quantify the relative influence of immediate and long-term prices [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: SiliconData's GPU price index overwhelmingly favors spot pricing rather than what companies pay on a long-term basis.

statement.excerpt: Yes, yes, I know, you’re going to tell me that SiliconData has an index, and that that index shows “GPU rental prices going up,” but these prices overwhelmingly favor spot pricing — as in what it costs to rent a GPU right now — versus what companies are paying on a long term basis.

from_speaker: what it costs to rent a GPU right now
versus what companies are paying on a long term basis
our_interpretation: Assess the index methodology in force at publication on October 13, 2026.
Read 'overwhelmingly' as a dominant preponderance of effective influence on the index. The speaker supplies no numerical threshold.
Use the speaker's definition of spot pricing, including immediately available rental prices, rather than restricting it to interruptible instances.
Including reserved prices does not by itself establish how much influence those prices have.
criteria.support_condition: Dated methodology, input composition and effective weights show that immediate rental prices dominate long-term contract prices in determining the index.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Those records show that long-term contract prices have substantial, comparable or dominant effective influence, inconsistent with overwhelming spot dominance.

evidence.explanation: The article describes coverage of on-demand, interruptible and reserved rentals, including commitments lasting up to 60 months. That cautions against treating the index as exclusively spot-based, but does not settle which inputs dominate.
